audit.report: A batch job (batch_replayable_price_sync, pid 102725) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4 seconds, blocking one session and contributing to checkout timeouts. Checkout success dropped to 8% over 30 seconds (100 of 109 failed) against a 95% SLO, putting ~$16,881/min of revenue at risk and exceeding the 60-second degradation tolerance. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker, but a prior memory (MEM-1) showed that terminating this same workload previously failed verification (29% checkout success vs 95% SLO). Both guardians agreed the decision required human judgment and escalated to the pricing team after 45.7 seconds. No automated action was executed.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_price_sync job (pid 102725) opened a transaction and went idle, holding a lock that blocked checkout sessions and caused widespread timeouts.
lessons: For batch_replayable_price_sync: add a pre-termination verification step that confirms checkout recovery before accepting termination, since MEM-1 proves termination alone did not restore the SLO last time.

For batch_replayable_price_sync: enforce a strict statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (e.g., ≤30s) so the job cannot hold locks idle long enough to breach the 60-second business tolerance.

For batch_replayable_price_sync: update the change calendar to include a maintenance window covering this job, so the Continuity Guardian can approve interruption without escalation when the workload is replayable and may_interrupt.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly used MEM-1 to anticipate that termination would not verify, and the Continuity Guardian accepted this evidence without objection; neither guardian wasted a round, but both deferred to escalation because the invariant (business verification required) could not be satisfied by the proposed action.
follow_ups: Pricing team: confirm whether batch_replayable_price_sync can be safely terminated now, and if not, identify the additional remediation (e.g., cache warm-up, dependency restart) needed for checkout to recover.
DBAs: deploy idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = 30s for the batch_worker role to prevent recurrence.
Platform team: add a change-calendar entry for batch_replayable_price_sync covering the may_interrupt policy so future negotiations can auto-approve.
